newsitem.title: UK: Scot Amicable to sell property investment business.
newsitem.headline: Scot Amicable to sell property investment business.

text.p: Scottish Amicable Investment Managers (SAIM) said on Tuesday it intended to sell its property investment management business to the Dutch mutual funds group Robeco.

SAIM's chief executive Douglas Ferrans told Reuters he could not disclose the sum being paid for the business which has been formed into a separate new company which will operate independently from its Glasgow base.
"The new company, Argyll Property Asset Management Ltd, is led by David Hunter and comprises the whole of the existing property management team," SAIM said in a statement.
SAIM said Argyll would have contracts to manage 1.7 billion stg of property assets for "a range of clients including the 950 million stg Scottish Amicable Life Fund Portfolio".

Ferrans said due diligence on the deal with the Robeco Group had been completed and the agreement was due to be completed on December 17. He said the property group, which has a staff of 42, would move "lock, stock and barrel" into the new company.

"Property has grown to a size which justifies its being on its own now," he added. He said the effective demerger allowed both Argyll and SAIM to "focus fully on their areas of expertise and places us in a strong position to fulfil our business aspirations".
Argyll's Hunter said in the same statement that the company would expanding its client base, adding that the link with Robeco "will bring...a wealth of contacts and ideas for the future".
